planted.note: jwt.decode() trusts the token payload without checking the HMAC, and src/server.js:56 falls back to identify() whenever verify() throws, so a self-minted token with any sub/org/role becomes the request principal.
The signing key falls back to a literal in the repository, so any deployment that misses JWT_SECRET signs and accepts tokens anyone reading the source can forge.

args.term is a GraphQL String interpolated straight into the ILIKE predicate, so a quote in the search box breaks out of the literal and appends arbitrary SQL to a query that already runs with the app's full database rights.
Every member record returned by orgMembers carries the live password-reset token, so any VIEWER in the org can read a colleague's reset token and take over their account.

The mutation checks only that the target shares the caller's org and never inspects ctx.user.role, so any authenticated member can deactivate the org owner; the restriction exists only in the console UI.

rejectUnauthorized:false disables chain verification on the Postgres connection, so anything able to sit between the API and the database can present its own certificate and read or rewrite every query.
The webhook shared secret is committed in the deployment template and injected into all three functions, so anyone with repository read access can forge delivery callbacks.
The inbound function is granted s3:* and secretsmanager:* on Resource '*', so a single code-execution bug in mail parsing yields every bucket and every secret in the account.
AuthType NONE publishes the render function on the open internet; the Cors block restricts browsers only, and any non-browser client can call the URL directly.

The URL comes from the attachmentUrls field of the notification payload and is fetched with no scheme or host check, so a crafted message makes the function retrieve internal endpoints including the instance metadata service.
The request body is compiled as a Jinja2 template, so a caller can walk the template sandbox's object graph to read files and run code inside the function.
messageKey is taken from the request and passed to get_object unscoped, so any caller can read any object in the mail store rather than only the message they were shown.

The filename comes from the MIME part or the notification payload and is joined to TMP_ROOT without normalisation, so ../../ segments write outside the scratch directory and can overwrite files in the function's runtime.
A callback with no X-Mailroom-Signature header is accepted as valid, so an attacker simply omits the header and writes arbitrary delivery-state records.
The Rack session cookie is signed with a literal in the repository, so anyone who reads it can mint a cookie for any uid, including an admin account.
params[:name] is joined to the uploads root and handed to send_file with no normalisation or prefix check, so ?name=../../../../etc/passwd serves arbitrary files readable by the process.
The post-login destination is taken from params[:next] with no check that it is a relative path, so a crafted login link lands a freshly authenticated user on an attacker-controlled host.
The search term is interpolated inside the LIKE literals of a statement built with no bind parameters, so a quote in ?q= lets the caller append arbitrary SQL and read other users' notes.
escape_html:false plus filter_html:false lets raw markup through the Markdown renderer, and views/note.erb:6 prints the result unescaped, so a script tag saved in a note runs for anyone who opens it.

Exposing every actuator endpoint puts /actuator/env, /actuator/heapdump and /actuator/loggers behind nothing more than an ordinary bearer token, so any tenant user can read the datasource password and dump process memory.
The H2 console is enabled and accepts remote connections, and SecurityConfig.java:70 permits it unauthenticated, giving anyone a JDBC console they can point at an arbitrary URL.
The production database password is committed in the default profile block, so it is available to everyone with repository access and to anyone who reaches /actuator/env.
The single-order read uses findById rather than findByIdAndOrgId, so any authenticated user can enumerate ids and read orders belonging to other organisations.
The whole request body is deserialised into the Order entity and written back, so a caller can set status and totalCents directly and mark an unpaid order DISPATCHED for zero.
The DocumentBuilderFactory keeps DTD processing on and turns entity expansion on explicitly, so an uploaded feed with a SYSTEM entity reads local files or forces outbound requests from the service.
A privileged container holds every capability and can mount host devices, so any code execution in the ledger process is a straight path to root on the node.

Mounting the node's docker socket into the pod hands the container the ability to start any container on that node, which is full node compromise and lateral movement across every workload scheduled there.
The built-in operator password is a literal in the manifest, so it is in the repository, in the rendered manifest and readable through the API by anyone able to get the Deployment.
Certificate checking is switched off for the clearing-house hop and passed to the container at deployment.yaml:53-54, so settlement traffic can be intercepted and altered by anything on that path.

The pprof and expvar handlers stay mounted by default and service.yaml:16-20 publishes the debug port on the Service, so anything in the cluster can pull heap and goroutine dumps containing in-flight ledger data.

Any page on any origin can open a message channel to the service worker, and background.js:54 runs the same privileged command set for external senders with no origin check, so a random site can capture the user's active tab.

planted.class: Exposure of resource to wrong sphere
planted.note: Every file in the extension, popup included, is fetchable by any page on any site, which both leaks the implementation and gives every visited page a stable extension id to fingerprint.

The debugger permission grants full DevTools protocol control of every tab, far beyond what a screenshot tool needs, so any compromise of the extension surface yields arbitrary script execution and cookie access on all sites.

The note is assigned with innerHTML into the visited page's DOM; the popup sanitises its own input but background.js:32-38 relays the same command from the external channel unfiltered, so any site can inject markup that executes in another site's page.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection through template-literal interpolation into an interval and a LIMIT
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/schema.graphql:44 declares eventBuckets(windowDays: Int!, limit: Int!), so GraphQL has already rejected anything that is not an integer before the resolver runs; src/resolvers/reports.js:25-26 then clamps both with Math.min.

decoys.looks_like: Origin reflection with credentials (permissive CORS)
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/server.js:82 mounts requireAllowedOrigin ahead of cors(corsOptions) at src/server.js:83, and requireAllowedOrigin (src/server.js:30-35) 403s any Origin outside config/default.json's allowedOrigins, so the reflected value can only ever be one of those two hosts.

decoys.looks_like: API key committed to the repository
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/analytics.js:6-10 documents it as the browser-shipped publishable key that only names the workspace, and src/analytics.js:12-17 shows every batch is authenticated by an HMAC over ANALYTICS_SECRET read from the environment, with a hard failure when it is absent.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection through string interpolation of a tenant name
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing in the tree calls it; the only other appearance of the name is the module.exports list at src/db.js:58, and both resolver modules import only { query } (src/resolvers/reports.js:3, src/resolvers/users.js:3).

decoys.looks_like: Privilege escalation - a caller-supplied role written straight into the users table
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/schema.graphql:51 types the argument as InviteRole!, and the enum at src/schema.graphql:3-6 contains only MEMBER and VIEWER, so no value that reaches the INSERT can grant more than the caller already has.

decoys.looks_like: Resolver with no authentication or authorization check that dereferences ctx.user
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/server.js:84 mounts requireSession in the /graphql chain before expressMiddleware, and requireSession (src/server.js:61-66) returns 401 whenever req.principal is unset, so no unauthenticated request reaches any resolver.

decoys.looks_like: Bucket policy granting s3:GetObject and s3:ListBucket to the world
decoys.ruled_out_by: The same statement carries a Condition at template.yaml:70-72 requiring aws:PrincipalOrgID to equal the OrgId parameter, so only principals inside the owning AWS organisation can match; PublicAccessBlockConfiguration at template.yaml:36-40 also has BlockPublicPolicy true.

decoys.looks_like: Path traversal - a request-supplied template name joined onto a directory
decoys.ruled_out_by: src/handlers/render.py:26-28 resolves the name through config.TEMPLATE_REGISTRY and raises KeyError on a miss, and that table (src/common/config.py:15-21) maps five fixed labels to five fixed filenames, so the value joined at line 29 is never caller-controlled.

decoys.looks_like: A 64-character HMAC secret hardcoded in a signature verifier
decoys.ruled_out_by: It is the carrier's published sandbox example, paired with the sandbox secret at tests/test_webhook.py:14 and exercised only by tests/test_webhook.py:21-26; the value actually used to verify is config.SIGNING_SECRET, read from the environment at src/common/config.py:8 and passed in at src/handlers/webhook.py:71.

decoys.looks_like: Code injection - eval() over a queue payload
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing calls it. The name appears exactly once in the tree, at its own definition (src/handlers/inbound.py:76); template.yaml wires only handlers.inbound.handler (template.yaml:84) as the function entry point.

decoys.looks_like: Lambda entry point with no authentication, signature check or caller validation
decoys.ruled_out_by: template.yaml:92-96 gives InboundFunction a single event source, the SNS topic, and unlike RenderFunction (template.yaml:107-113) it has no FunctionUrlConfig and no Api event, so it has no internet-reachable invocation path to authenticate.

decoys.looks_like: Cross-site scripting - a session-derived value printed with the unescaped <%== %> tag
decoys.ruled_out_by: take_notice (app.rb:45-48) uses the session value only as a lookup key into the frozen NOTICES hash (app.rb:25-32) and returns nil for anything absent, so the string rendered is always one of six literals written in the source.

decoys.looks_like: Admin route with no role check in the handler
decoys.ruled_out_by: The before '/admin/*' filter at app.rb:61-64 runs first and halts with 403 unless current_user['role'] == 'admin', so the handler body is only reached by an admin.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection - LIMIT and OFFSET spliced into the statement
decoys.ruled_out_by: app.rb:106-110 is the only caller: limit comes from Integer(), which raises on anything non-numeric, and is then clamped to 1..100, and offset is computed arithmetically from a to_i page number, so both are Ruby Integers.

decoys.looks_like: Command injection - an interpolated path passed to system()
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing calls it; the name occurs only at its definition (lib/attachments.rb:26), and app.rb's upload route uses Attachments.store (app.rb:142).

decoys.looks_like: CSRF protection disabled on a state-changing API
decoys.ruled_out_by: The next line sets SessionCreationPolicy.STATELESS (SecurityConfig.java:66) and the only credential the server reads is the Authorization bearer header (SecurityConfig.java:77-88), with no form login, no httpBasic and no cookie authentication anywhere in the tree, so there is no ambient credential a cross-site request could ride on.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection - a status value concatenated into the WHERE clause
decoys.ruled_out_by: The parameter is typed OrderStatus (OrderRepository.java:63) and the enum in src/main/java/io/orderbook/model/OrderStatus.java:8-16 declares seven constants, so name() can only ever return one of those seven identifiers; Spring rejects any other ?status= value before the controller (OrderController.java:46).

decoys.looks_like: CORS configured to allow any origin
decoys.ruled_out_by: It sits in the document fragment guarded by spring.config.activate.on-profile: local (application.yml:63-67), while the active profile is prod (application.yml:5); the prod block sets two explicit hosts (application.yml:52-55) and the registry never enables credentials (OrderbookApplication.java:24-28).

decoys.looks_like: JWT claims parsed without verifying the signature
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing calls it. The argument resolver registered at SecurityConfig.java:116-130 delegates to resolve() (SecurityConfig.java:128), which verifies with the key at SecurityConfig.java:83, and the deprecated method's name appears nowhere else in the tree.

decoys.looks_like: Bulk export endpoint with no role check, despite the javadoc calling it staff-only
decoys.ruled_out_by: SecurityConfig.java:71 matches GET /api/orders/export with hasRole("OPS") in the filter chain, so a non-OPS caller is rejected before the handler is entered.

decoys.looks_like: SQL injection - a LIMIT value concatenated into the statement
decoys.ruled_out_by: The parameter is a Java int (OrderRepository.java:70), so no non-numeric value can reach the concatenation; both call sites bound it as well (OrderController.java:53 clamps to 200, OrderController.java:101 passes the configured max-rows int).

decoys.looks_like: RBAC rule granting read access to Secrets
decoys.ruled_out_by: The same rule pins resourceNames to .Values.rbac.secretName (templates/rbac.yaml:21-22, values.yaml:28), so it covers exactly the one Secret the pod boots from; it is a namespaced Role, and the verbs exclude list.

decoys.looks_like: Service account token automatically mounted into every pod that uses it
decoys.ruled_out_by: templates/deployment.yaml:31 sets automountServiceAccountToken: false on the pod spec, and the pod-level field overrides the service-account default, so the ledger pods never receive the token.

decoys.looks_like: NetworkPolicy admitting an entire namespace via namespaceSelector
decoys.ruled_out_by: The namespaceSelector and the podSelector at templates/networkpolicy.yaml:20-22 are keys of a single list element, which is one peer with both conditions ANDed, not two OR'd peers, so only gateway pods inside the platform namespace match.

decoys.looks_like: Secret material base64-encoded into a committed manifest
decoys.ruled_out_by: The value decodes to the ASCII string "placeholder-replaced-by-vault-injector" (and clearing-token at line 17 to "not-a-real-token-see-vault-path"), and the annotations at templates/secret.yaml:7-13 show the agent injector rewrites both keys on admission from the Vault path.

decoys.looks_like: Privileged pod spec with hostPID, hostNetwork and the node root filesystem mounted
decoys.ruled_out_by: No template includes it: the string breakGlassPodSpec appears only at its own define (templates/_helpers.tpl:22), and Helm never renders a define that is not included, so nothing in the chart emits this pod.

decoys.looks_like: A message-supplied string reaching document.querySelector as a selector
decoys.ruled_out_by: target is used only as a key into CLIP_TARGETS (lib/allowlist.js:9-16), which maps six fixed labels to six fixed selectors, and an unknown label returns document.body at content.js:7-9, so the selector string never comes from the message.

decoys.looks_like: Cleartext transmission of captured page data to a caller-supplied host
decoys.ruled_out_by: Nothing calls it; the name occurs only at its definition (lib/sync.js:46), and background.js routes the push command to pushClip (background.js:28), which resolves the endpoint from the two https URLs in SYNC_ENDPOINTS (lib/allowlist.js:19-22) and throws on anything else.

decoys.looks_like: Cross-site scripting - innerHTML assembled from page-controlled tab title and URL
decoys.ruled_out_by: Both interpolated values are wrapped in escapeHtml at popup.js:24, defined at popup.js:5-12, and the only unescaped value, clip.dataUrl, is produced by chrome.tabs.captureVisibleTab in background.js:6-8 rather than by the page.
